title: Rectangular matrix multiplication: arithmetic exponent over a field

model.instance: All inputs are explicit: $A\in\mathbb F^{n_1\times n_2},B\in\mathbb F^{n_2\times n_3}$; $(n_1,n_2,n_3)=(\lceil n^{a}\rceil,\lceil n^{b}\rceil,\lceil n^{c}\rceil)$.

assumptions.description: All input entries may be read; there is no black-box matrix-vector restriction.

model.parameter_domain_description: n>=1 and n tends to infinity; field F and shape exponents a>=b>=c>0 are fixed in advance and independent of n.
model.description_zh: Assume $A\in\mathbb F^{\lceil n^a\rceil\times\lceil n^b\rceil}$ and $B\in\mathbb F^{\lceil n^b\rceil\times\lceil n^c\rceil}$. The field $\mathbb F$ and real shape exponents $a\ge b\ge c>0$ are fixed in advance, with $n\to\infty$.

proofs.title: A flattening lower bound for the matrix-multiplication tensor.
proofs.body: For multiplying an n^a by n^b matrix by an n^b by n^c matrix, the three flattening ranks of the matrix-multiplication tensor have exponents a+b, b+c, and a+c. Tensor rank is at least their maximum. Under a>=b>=c>0 this maximum is a+b. Bilinearization changes arithmetic complexity by only a constant factor, so omega_F(a,b,c)>=a+b.
proofs.scope: All model, oracle, algorithm, guarantee, quantity, resource-projection, and region conditions attached to the mapped bounds remain in force.

evidence.location: A flattening lower bound for the matrix-multiplication tensor.

evidence.supports: Fix shape exponents $a\ge b\ge c>0$. If $c(a+b)\le ab$, the rectangular multiplication exponent is exactly $\omega_{\mathbb F}(a,b,c)=a+b$. If $c(a+b)>ab$, the recorded bracket is $a+b\le\omega_{\mathbb F}(a,b,c)\le(ab+bc+ca)^2/(4abc)$. These statements compare asymptotic arithmetic exponents; an infimum exponent does not by itself give an endpoint operation bound $O(n^\omega)$.
